By Jon Healy

By Henry Hanson

Topic:Cricket

Australia is pushing towards a big lead in Durban despite losing regular wickets on day four, with Matt Renshaw once again looking composed at the crease after Nic Maddinson's quickfire 48.

Matt Renshaw is once again looking composed at the crease after Nic Maddinson's quickfire 48.

Follow all the action in our live blog below, keep up with all the stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio call on the ABC Listen app.

By Jon Healy

Choose what information you see below by using filters

All

55

Key Events

7

Wickets

4

By Henry Hanson

Webster works a single and before Renshaw defends a couple.

50 for Matt Renshaw! The southpaw is down and reverse sweeping and profiting with a boundary.

How good.

By Henry Hanson

Nortje is dangling one outside off and Renshaw is patting it into the turf.

On the hip and the Aussie is fluently turning it for a single.

Edge! But safe. Webster's nick was hurtling towards earth quickly and falls a couple metres short of the cordon.

Webster is then deflecting backward of point for a single — he loves that shot.

Renshaw gets one on the pads and works it through midwicket. The batters are back for a couple to end the over.

By Henry Hanson

And the new batter is Beau Webster — he could certainly do with a score.

But it's Matt Renshaw facing the first ball of the over.

He's working a single into the on-side.

Webster is back and confidently defending his first ball.

The big man is then down and sweeping but finding an infielder. No run.

Key Event

By Henry Hanson

Carey is driving on the up but only getting a toe edge on the ball, sending it bouncing into his stumps.

That's another wicket for the lionhearted Anrich Nortje.

Carey departs for 24 just as he was threatening to really launch.

Australia 5-205 and 311 runs in front.

By Henry Hanson

Things are moving really slowly out there at the moment.

There seems to be an age passing between overs as the Aussies just tick along.

Shot! Carey is driving attractively through the off-side and Wiaan Mulder is in pursuit. Mulder pulls out a despairing dive with the ball inches from the rope, and it's in vain.

It looks like Mulder, who proceeded to crash into the advertising hoarding, has done a bit of damage here. He's holding his shoulder as he gets up gingerly.

More runs! This time, it's an upper cut from Carey. Lovely stuff and another boundary.

By Henry Hanson

Renshaw pushes a single and there it is — Australia now leads by 300.

Harmer extracts some sharp turn, but Renshaw is playing inside the line.

Another quick single from the Aussies.

Four singles from the over.

By Henry Hanson

Nortje is getting shoes looked at, or strapped up or something, and there's a lengthy pause between overs.

Eventually, Nortje is ready to begin the third over of his spell.

Shout! Nortje is hitting Carey on the pad but it's a very quick shake of the head from the umpire. The replays show Carey got a big inside edge on the ball.

Carey pushes sweetly through cover for a couple.

He's then wafting at one outside off.

By Henry Hanson

Renshaw nudges a single into the leg side.

Carey returns the favour.

Singles on offer absolutely everywhere at the moment.

Renshaw is driving fluently but only finding Temba Bavuma at cover. No run.

Very slow and very wide from Harmer — Renshaw leaves it alone.

Again, very wide and very, very slow — this one is only 74km/hr.

Renshaw has all the time in the world to decide not to play at it.

By Henry Hanson

He's angling across Carey, who's using soft hands to nudge a single through point.

Renshaw is shouldering arms outside off.

Edge! But safe! Renshaw is squared up and edging directly between second slip and gully. The ball races to the boundaries and there are a couple South African fielders on their haunches.

Painful stuff. That would have been a regulation grab for a third slip.

Renshaw pushes into the on-side and the batters hustle back for a well-run two.

A quick single ends the over.

By Henry Hanson

Slow and loopy from Harmer, and Renshaw is beaten by some sharp turn from the rough.

The Australian is then down and reverse-sweeping for a single.

Carey is forward and defending.

He then squirts out an inside edge into the leg-side and the batters run a single to end the over.

By Henry Hanson

The South African spearhead is angling across Renshaw, who takes one off his pads and works a single behind square.

Shot! Oh my goodness, Alex Carey has absolutely creamed Nortje through extra cover. That's a beautifully timed drive and the Aussies have their first boundary of the session.

Nortje is testing Carey with a bouncer, which the Australian wicketkeeper is underneath.

Shout! Carey is hit on the front pad but that looked like it pitched outside leg.

Temba Bavuma trusts the umpire's decision of not out.

By Henry Hanson

What are we looking at for a declaration - runs? Overs remaining?

- Mick

Given that we'll probably only see half an hour of play in today and tomorrow's evening sessions, if I was Pat Cummins, I'd be wanting to be bowling before tea.

That would give the Australians about three, three and a half sessions to take ten wickets.

The Aussies lead by 280 right now, so I reckon they'll be looking to be around 350-380 in front by then.

Either way, we're set for some fireworks after lunch, with the Aussies in search of quick runs.

Key Event

By Jon Healy

A mixed session with Australia losing four wickets, but also going at almost five an over.

They lead by 280 so can bat for an hour, maybe a little longer after lunch before declaring with a 350-run lead.

At least, I think that will be the plan, but the South African bowlers will have a bit to say about that. Can they cause a collapse and keep the target within reason?

We'll find out a little later.

By Jon Healy

How kind of him.

What a shot! Harmer throws it miles down the leg side and Renshaw somehow manufactures a reverse sweep through cover for four.

Harmer is over the wicket, so Renshaw is padding up and just keeping them out here.

He looks to go the reverse sweep again, but pulls out as the line or speed isn't quite right for him.

He finds the single to cover more conventionally. So Alex Carey will face the last ball before lunch after a long readjustment of the field.

BEATEN! What a ball to beat the outside edge to end the session.

The umpires are having a look at a potential stumping, but Carey never lifted his foot.

By Jon Healy

Nortje starts by firing in a yorker that Carey digs out.

The way he bats with his hands away from his body, Carey always looks a threat of nicking off or chopping on to pace. If Nortje can stay in that fifth stump area, he will always be in the game.

Carey manages to find a single with a little dink to the vacant point region.

And Renshaw finds the space too as he jumps and clips a shortish ball off his hip to deep fine leg.

By Jon Healy

Renshaw is almost burned by Alex Carey! Renshaw clips to mid-on and calls "noYeah yeah yeah", taking off for a single before being sent back by Carey. He gets back comfortably, but there was probably a single in that.

Harmer is keeping these batters, both excellent players of spin honest. Just two singles from the over.

By Jon Healy

And Alex Carey clips off his hip to start the over with a single.

Nortje's first to Renshaw is more hostile, short and down leg. The bouncers ruffled Renshaw a little in the first dig, so this isn't a bad tactic.

Renshaw pushes into the deep on the off side and thinks about two but decides against it as Keshav Maharaj comes in off the rope.

Gorgeous from Nortje as he seams across Alex Carey to beat the outside edge. What a ball to the new batter.

By Jon Healy

The off spinner is looking really tough to play out there right now. Nathan Lyon is licking his lips, but Australia's lead is still only 267 runs, so the batters still have some work to do.

A couple more singles to the tally, but the decisive boundaries have dried up.

By Jon Healy

No slips in place for Keshav Maharaj an over after getting a wicket. A fascinating decision.

Almost bowled him! Renshaw goes for the lap sweep and gets barely anything on it to the point it almost rolls back onto the stumps. Renshaw ends up diving to put his body between the ball and the pegs.

Both these batters will sweep and reverse sweep all the live long day.

Just three runs off the over though.
